angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 893,975 km at 199.65 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.0088 +/- 0.0203 mas (same row, RUWE 0.83): 199.65 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.285 +/- 0.051 solar radii from Turner et al. 2016, the stellar radius of WASP-123 b's parameter set from Turner et al. 2016 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016PASP..128f4401T/abstract): 893,975 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.166 +/- 0.061 solar masses from Turner et al. 2016, the stellar mass of WASP-123 b's parameter set from Turner et al. 2016 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016PASP..128f4401T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5740 +/- 130 K from Turner et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of WASP-123 b's parameter set from Turner et al. 2016 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016PASP..128f4401T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Turner et al. 2016, the stellar temperature of WASP-123 b's parameter set from Turner et al. 2016 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2016PASP..128f4401T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-123.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.287, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
